report.summary: Enumerated symbols and claims in daedalus/structcore/metrics.py chunk 1 of 1.
risks: _count_comments | medium | Block comment parsing for non-Python languages is simplistic and may miscount (e.g., block comment markers inside strings). | Verify against a corpus of multi-language files with block comments.
_lizard_cc | low | Returns None on any exception; silent failure may hide issues. | Add logging or specific exception handling.
file_metrics | low | guard_density uses guard_count / loc; guard_count may double-count if guard_keywords overlap. | Review guard_keywords definitions in LanguageSpec.

handoff.purpose: Compute per-file health metrics (LOC, comment density, guard density, long functions, optional cyclomatic complexity via lizard).

symbols.name: lizard_available
symbols.note: Returns True if lizard can be imported, else False; cached with maxsize=1.

symbols.name: file_metrics
symbols.note: Main entry: computes dict of metrics for a file given module, text, LanguageSpec, and list of CodeUnit.

symbols.name: _count_comments
symbols.note: Counts comment lines: uses tokenize for Python, otherwise line-based block/line comment detection.

symbols.name: _count_guards
symbols.note: Counts occurrences of guard_keywords from LanguageSpec using regex for alphabetic keywords, else str.count.

symbols.name: _lizard_cc
symbols.note: Returns dict with cc_avg and cc_max from lizard analysis, or None if not available or fails.

claims.text: Per-file health metrics — the 'code health' signal, comment-aware per language.
claims.why: The module provides per-file metrics including comment_density, which is comment-aware and uses language-specific comment detection.

claims.text: Stdlib-only baseline (LOC, function count, comment density, guard/over-defensive density, long-function flag).
claims.why: file_metrics returns loc, n_functions (function count), comment_density, guard_density, guard_count, long_functions. No external libraries are required for these.

claims.text: If ``lizard`` is installed, real cyclomatic complexity (avg/max) is added for the languages lizard supports.
claims.why: lizard_available() checks for lizard; file_metrics calls _lizard_cc which uses lizard.analyze_file.analyze_source_code and returns cc_avg and cc_max.

claims.text: _LONG_FN = 60
claims.why: Constant defined as 60.

claims.text: @lru_cache(maxsize=1) def lizard_available():
claims.why: Function is decorated with lru_cache(maxsize=1).

claims.text: def file_metrics(module: str, text: str, spec: LanguageSpec, units: list[CodeUnit]) -> dict:
claims.why: Function signature matches; returns a dict.

claims.text: lines = text.splitlines() / loc = len(lines)
claims.why: Code does exactly that.

claims.text: comment_lines = _count_comments(text, spec)
claims.why: Calls _count_comments with text and spec.

claims.text: guard = _count_guards(text, spec)
claims.why: Calls _count_guards with text and spec.

claims.text: long_fns = [{"name": u.name, "line": u.line, "loc": u.loc} for u in units if u.loc > _LONG_FN]
claims.why: List comprehension filters units with loc > 60.

claims.text: metrics = { "language": spec.name, "loc": loc, "n_functions": len(units), "comment_density": round(comment_lines / max(loc, 1), 3), "guard_density": round(guard / max(loc, 1), 3), "guard_count": guard, "long_functions": long_fns }
claims.why: Dictionary is built exactly as shown.

claims.text: cc = _lizard_cc(module, text) if lizard_available() else None
claims.why: Conditional assignment as described.

claims.text: if cc: metrics.update(cc)
claims.why: Updates metrics if cc is truthy (non-None dict).

claims.text: def _count_comments(text: str, spec: LanguageSpec) -> int:
claims.why: Function signature present.

claims.text: if spec.name == "python": n = 0; try: for tok in tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(text).readline): if tok.type == tokenize.COMMENT: n += 1; except (tokenize.TokenError, IndentationError): pass; return n
claims.why: Code uses tokenize for Python and returns count.

claims.text: n = 0; in_block = False; block = spec.block_comment[0] if spec.block_comment else None
claims.why: Initialization as described.

claims.text: for raw in text.splitlines(): line = raw.strip(); if in_block: n += 1; if block and block[1] in line: in_block = False; continue; if block and block[0] in line and block[1] not in line: in_block = True; n += 1; continue; if any(line.startswith(m) for m in spec.line_comment) or (block and block[0] in line): n += 1
claims.why: Line-based comment counting logic matches the description.

claims.text: def _count_guards(text: str, spec: LanguageSpec) -> int:
claims.why: Function signature present.

claims.text: n = 0; for kw in spec.guard_keywords: if kw.isalpha(): n += len(re.findall(rf"\b{re.escape(kw)}\b", text)); else: n += text.count(kw); return n
claims.why: Code counts guard keywords as described.

claims.text: def _lizard_cc(module: str, text: str) -> dict | None:
claims.why: Function signature present.

claims.text: import lizard; ext = "." + module.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if "." in module else ".txt"; try: analysis = lizard.analyze_file.analyze_source_code(module, text); except Exception: return None; ccs = [f.cyclomatic_complexity for f in analysis.function_list]; if not ccs: return None; return {"cc_avg": round(sum(ccs) / len(ccs), 1), "cc_max": max(ccs)}
claims.why: Code imports lizard, attempts analysis, computes averages and returns dict or None.

observations.what: The module docstring claims 'comment-aware per language', but the comment counting logic for non-Python languages is simplistic and may miscount block comments that span multiple lines or appear inside strings.
lizard_available() caches the result with maxsize=1, so if lizard is not installed at first call, subsequent calls will not retry even if lizard becomes available.
_lizard_cc constructs an extension ext but never uses it; the variable is dead code.
file_metrics returns a dict with keys 'cc_avg' and 'cc_max' only if lizard analysis succeeds; otherwise those keys are absent. This may surprise callers expecting them always.
